messages:
samir: Morning team — our CI started failing when exchanging the GitHub Actions OIDC token for a Redwood CI token. The workflow hits our exchange endpoint and we get a 401. Happening in two repos after we migrated org names.

samir: Quick curl from the runner: 
```
TOKEN=$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/auth/oidc/exchange
# -> 401 {\"error\":\"invalid_token\", \"message\":\"token audience mismatch\"}
```

infra-bot: Alert: 2 failed deploys detected (repo-x, repo-y) within 12m. Tag: ci/oidc.

maria: Can you paste the decoded JWT claims (header+payload)? That error usually means aud/issuer mismatch with our provider config.

samir: Payload (sanitized):
```
{
  \"aud\": \"sts.amazonaws.com\",
  \"iss\": \"https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com\",
  \"sub\": \"repo:example-org/repo-x:ref:refs/heads/main\",
  \"exp\": 1719901234
}
```

jess: As suspected — GitHub default aud is sts.amazonaws.com. Our OIDC validation expects aud to be https://redwood-oauth.internal (we enforce exact match). In GH Actions you must request id-token with a specific audience in the step.

oncall-sre: Also verify token TTL. If our exchange expects token TTL > time-to-exchange we sometimes see expiry during long runners. Share the action step.

samir: This is the step we used (we omitted audience):
```
- name: Acquire id-token
  id: idtoken
  uses: actions/oidc@v1
```

maria: Update to explicitly set audience: 
```
- name: Acquire id-token
  id: idtoken
  uses: actions/oidc@v1
  with:
    audience: 'https://redwood-oauth.internal'
```
And ensure permissions:
```
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read
```

samir: Did that — token now decodes to correct aud. But the exchange returns 403: "insufficient_scope: required=deploy:write" when requesting the CI token.

jess: That indicates our mapping layer didn't grant that scope. We validate repo allowlist (sub) and then issue a CI token containing granted scopes. If the repo name changed during org migration, mapping could be missing. The OIDC token itself doesn't carry arbitrary scopes; you request desired scopes when calling our exchange endpoint but our backend checks allowlist/role mapping first.

samir: Our exchange request (from workflow):
```
POST /v1/auth/oidc/exchange
Auth: Bearer <OIDC_TOKEN>
Body: {\"requested_scopes\": [\"deploy:write\"]}
```

oncall-sre: Looking at auth logs: 'repo mapping not found' for "example-org/repo-x" around line 612. Did the repo get re-registered after the org rename?

samir: We did an org rename/move last month; I think I missed re-adding repo-x to our OIDC allowlist.

maria: Two-step plan: (1) short-term: create a temporary CI API key scoped to deploy:write and restrict it to GitHub runner IP ranges / tag it ephemeral. Use it to unblock deploys. (2) long-term: add the new repo name to the OIDC allowlist and update internal onboarding to include post-move steps.

samir: Temporary key created with TTL 12h and tag ephemeral=true. Deploys succeeded. Opened ticket RED-4021 to re-add repos and update docs.

jess: For the ticket, add a unit/CI check in our GH Action templates that validates the id-token aud and that the repo is present in allowlist via a quick call to a read-only endpoint. Example quick verification step: 
```
- run: |
    echo $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN | awk -F\".\" '{print $2}' | base64 --decode | jq .aud
```

oncall-sre: Security note: avoid broad scopes on temporary keys. Use least-privilege (e.g., deploy:staging:create) and ensure automated revocation if TTL not honored. Tagging ephemeral keys triggers our revocation lambda after 48h.

customer-ops-bot: Audit event recorded (evt=api_key.create, actor=samir, ttl=12h, note=ephemeral workaround). Forwarded to sec-ops.

maria: Also update the OIDC trust config docs to show the exact audience string and to remind users to include id-token: write permission in the workflow.

samir: Thanks, everyone — root cause: missing allowlist entry after repo migration and missing audience param in workflow. Fixes applied: added audience, created ephemeral key to restore immediate operations, ticket RED-4021 created to remediate and harden templates. Monitoring deploys for next 24h. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Auto-close: incident resolved (reason: config + allowlist fix). Related ticket: RED-4021.
